name: InterContinental Sydney
positioning: Harbourside luxury hotel at Circular Quay, set within Sydney's restored 1851 Treasury Building
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to the Opera House, Harbour Bridge and Royal Botanic Gardens
Guests who want harbour or Opera House views from their room, pool or club lounge

facts.text: The hotel is set within the restored Treasury Building of 1851.
The Treasury Building was the first purpose-built government office in Sydney.
The building houses the oldest operating lift in the Southern Hemisphere and the first vault in Australia.
The hotel sits in the dress circle of Circular Quay, with views across the harbour.
Guest rooms have views of Sydney Harbour Bridge, Sydney Opera House, the Royal Botanic Gardens or the city skyline.
The heated indoor pool sits 31 stories high, with views of the Sydney Opera House through glass windows.
Guests can walk to the Sydney Opera House, Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Royal Botanic Gardens and The Rocks historic quarter.
The Club InterContinental lounge has views of Sydney Harbour, the Opera House and the Royal Botanic Garden from high above.
Aster is the hotel's rooftop bar, with expansive harbour views and creative cocktails.
Rooms have a window-side chaise, a dedicated work station and Byredo bath amenities.
Suites include the Governor Opera Suite, the Royal Opera Suite and the Presidential Opera Suite.
Conde Nast Traveler notes a calm palette of blues and grays that enhances the connection to the harbour, and marble-clad bathrooms.

highlights.text: A heated indoor pool 31 stories up, looking out to the Sydney Opera House through glass windows.
Set within the restored Treasury Building of 1851, which houses the oldest operating lift in the Southern Hemisphere and the first vault in Australia.
Guest rooms look out to Sydney Harbour Bridge, Sydney Opera House, the Royal Botanic Gardens or the city skyline.
The Club InterContinental lounge overlooks Sydney Harbour, the Opera House and the Royal Botanic Garden from high above.
Aster, the rooftop bar, pairs expansive harbour views with creative cocktails.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes guests need to go off-site for spa services.
Pets are not permitted, though guide dogs and service animals are welcome.
WhataHotel notes a busy tourist area with high foot traffic.
